baselineThesis.summary: Costco compounds through traffic-led comparable sales and membership fee income; valuation leaves little room for a comp slowdown.

baselineThesis.authorshipLabel: Demo-authored thesis anchored to Costco's FY2026 Q3 release (8-K filed 2026-05-28). Not a real institution's view; not investment advice.

proposals.headline: Close Q4 net sales growth forecast as a beat
proposals.whatChanged: Costco reported Q4 FY2026 net sales growth of 11.2 percent versus our 9 percent base case, a beat of just over two percentage points. The period matches the 16-week fourth quarter ended August 30, 2026.
proposals.againstOurView: Prior view (T-E004) was 9 percent Q4 FY2026 net sales growth.
proposals.whyItMatters: The sales beat reduces near-term concern that Costco’s comp engine is slowing. It also raises the bar for FY2027 expectations given the valuation risk tied to any deceleration.
uncertainties: The release does not disclose traffic versus ticket, so it does not fully prove the traffic-led component of the comp thesis.
Sustaining this growth rate into FY2027 depends on management commentary and monthly sales trends.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Update the Q4 forecast record and review call commentary for traffic, ticket, and early FY2027 trends.

proposals.headline: Close Q4 net income forecast as a slight reported beat
proposals.whatChanged: Costco reported Q4 FY2026 net income of $2.998 billion versus our $2.95 billion base case, a slight beat of less than one tenth of a billion dollars. The period matches the 16-week fourth quarter ended August 30, 2026, but EPS included a $0.15 non-recurring tariff refund benefit.
proposals.againstOurView: Prior view (T-E005) was $2.95 billion of Q4 FY2026 net income.
proposals.whyItMatters: Reported earnings cleared the forecast, but the one-time tariff refund means the run-rate earnings power may be lower than the headline result implies.
uncertainties: The release does not quantify the net income impact of the tariff refund separately from the EPS disclosure.
Management commentary is needed to assess how much benefit was reinvested in member value.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Close the forecast on reported GAAP net income and isolate the tariff refund impact when updating FY2027 earnings assumptions.

proposals.headline: Close Q4 EPS forecast as a reported beat, with quality caveat
proposals.whatChanged: Costco reported Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS of $6.75 versus our $6.65 base case, a beat of ten cents. The period matches the 16-week fourth quarter ended August 30, 2026, but $0.15 per share came from a non-recurring tariff refund benefit.
proposals.againstOurView: Prior view (T-E006) was $6.65 of Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS.
proposals.whyItMatters: The reported EPS beat is positive, but the non-recurring refund benefit is larger than the beat. That makes underlying EPS quality the key follow-up before raising forward earnings power.
uncertainties: Whether the tariff refund benefit recurs or reverses is not answered in the release.
The release does not quantify the amount reinvested in member values.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Close the EPS forecast on reported diluted EPS, but adjust the forward model after the call for any non-recurring tariff refund impact.

proposals.headline: Put membership fee growth pillar into review
proposals.whatChanged: Membership fees in the 16-week quarter grew about 7% while net sales grew 11.2%; for the 52-week year, membership fees grew about 11% versus sales up 10.1%. That mixed cadence puts the “faster than sales” pillar into review rather than cleanly confirming it.
proposals.againstOurView: Prior view (T-E002) was that the fee increase keeps membership fee income growing faster than sales.
proposals.whyItMatters: Membership fee income is a high-quality earnings stream; if it is not consistently outgrowing sales after the fee increase, the earnings-compounding case is less clean.
uncertainties: Q4 may be affected by timing of fee recognition versus the fee increase rollout.
Renewal rates, member counts, and executive member mix are not disclosed in the release.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Review call commentary for membership renewal rates, fee increase recognition timing, and whether Q4 fee growth should reaccelerate.

proposals.headline: Create follow-up on non-recurring tariff refund benefit
proposals.whatChanged: Reported Q4 EPS included a $0.15 per diluted share non-recurring benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, after partial reinvestment in member values. The release does not quantify the gross refund, reinvestment, or future reversal risk.
proposals.againstOurView: Prior risk (T-E007) focused on tariffs pressuring merchandise margins if import costs could not be passed through.
proposals.whyItMatters: The tariff item flips the near-term impact from pressure to benefit, but it may not be durable. The team needs to separate underlying margin from one-time refund and reinvestment effects.
uncertainties: Gross refund amount is not disclosed.
Partial reinvestment amount is not disclosed.
Whether any benefit or reversal carries into future quarters is not disclosed.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Ask management to quantify the tariff refund, reinvestment in member value, and expected impact on merchandise margins after Q4.

value.question: How much of the Q4 IEEPA tariff refund benefit flowed through merchandise margin, how much was reinvested in member value, and what reverses after Q4 FY2026?

Exhibit 99.1 Press Release
COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS

ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation ("Costco" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.

Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:

16 Weeks | 16 Weeks | 52 Weeks | 52 Weeks
Adjusted* | Adjusted*
U.S. | 10.7% | 7.2% | 8.2% | 6.6%
Canada | 5.0% | 4.6% | 7.8% | 6.7%
Other International | 7.0% | 6.2% | 9.8% | 6.5%
Total Company | 9.4% | 6.7% | 8.4% | 6.6%
Digitally-Enabled | 19.5% | 19.8% | 20.9% | 20.7%
*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange.

Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values. Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.

Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.
A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. (PT) today, September 24, 2026, and will be available via a webcast on investor.costco.com (click "Events & Presentations").
